STOODY.note: K printed as .2610 (the same as G; out of sequence between J .2770 and L .2900). O printed as .3150. Metric list read where an inch value was printed on the same line; 9.8 appears twice (against .3504 and .3858), the first is taken as a misprint of 8.9.

OPTIMAS_M.note: Lists ISO 261 sizes including second and third choices; fine list read to M24 x 1.5. Basic dimensions printed: M17x1 d3 printed 15.733 (formula 15.773) and M48 D1 printed 42.857 (formula 42.587) look like transpositions; all other checked values agree with ISO 68-1 formulas to 0.001 mm. Its tap drill column is major minus pitch.

WIKI_UTS.title: Unified Thread Standard (main size table)
WIKI_UTS.note: Number-size formula printed: major diameter = number x 0.013 in + 0.060 in. Names ASME B1.1-2024.

OPTIMAS_TOL.note: Header note 'Tolerances 6g (6h)'; M1 to M1.4 are printed with zero allowance (6h). M2.5 pitch max printed 2.118 (Ganter and the formula: 2.188).

GANTER_13.title: Metric ISO threads, tolerance fields 6g / 6H (DIN 13 extract, technical information 2393)

GANTER_IT.title: DIN ISO 286 ISO-Grundtoleranzen, Auszug Teil 1 Zahlenwerte (technical appendix p. 2150)
GANTER_IT.note: Printed in um with decimal commas. IT18 over 315 to 400 printed as 2200, out of sequence with its neighbours (8100, 9700); recorded as printed.

GOST_25346.title: GOST 25346-89 Unified system of tolerances and fits, Tables 2 and 3 (national adoption of ISO 286-1:1988)

ROYMECH.title: ISO shaft fundamental deviations 0 to 500 mm
ROYMECH.note: The site does not permit substantial reproduction, so its table is not republished here. It was compared value by value with the GOST 25346 transcription for letters a to zc (except j, js, k): all 517 printed values are equal. Only its k column is recorded.

SIMPLYB.title: FAQ / ISO 286 Limits and Fits reference (shaft and hole limit deviations, ISO 286-2)
SIMPLYB.note: Prints limit deviations of tolerance classes for 3 to 400 mm. The fundamental deviation is read as the limit nearest zero of the class named in 'from'. f6 over 120 to 180 printed -43/-48 (lower limit inconsistent with f5/f7; the upper, fundamental, value -43 is unaffected).

OSG_JIS.title: Deviation of shafts to be used in commonly used fits (JIS B 0401 extract)
OSG_JIS.note: JIS B 0401 is the Japanese adoption of ISO 286. Prints limit deviations up to 250 mm; fundamental deviation read as the limit nearest zero.

WIKI_BSP.title: British Standard Pipe (size table)
WIKI_BSP.note: Names ISO 7-1:1994 and ISO 228-1:2000. Prints TPI, pitch, major and minor diameter (in and mm), gauge length and tapping drills.

ETB_BSP.title: ISO 228 - Pipe threads where pressure tight joints are not made on the threads
ETB_BSP.note: Major diameter printed to 0.01 mm, G 1/8 to G 4. Its "minor (nut) diameter" column is not the basic minor diameter (it is larger), so it is not compared.

WIKI_NPT.title: National pipe thread (NPT dimensions table)
WIKI_NPT.note: Names ASME B1.20.1 without a year. The 4 1/2 row is printed without engagement values. 1/16 OD printed .313; E1 is reproduced with 0.3125.

UWASHER_NPT.title: NPT basic dimensions chart (reproduces the ANSI B2.1-1968 table)
UWASHER_NPT.note: Equipment retailer; table credited to ANSI B2.1-1968, the predecessor of ASME B1.20.1. 1/16 OD printed .313. 4 in E1 printed 4.38712 (Wikipedia 4.38713; exact value 4.387125).

WIKI_BSW.title: British Standard Whitworth (BSW size table)
WIKI_BSW.note: Names BS 84:2007. Prints the profile constants 55 deg, depth 0.640327p, radius 0.137329p.

EE_WHIT.title: Whitworth British screw threads size chart, BSW and BSF
EE_WHIT.note: Sizes printed as "11/8" etc. read as 1 1/8. Checked against the BS 84 profile formulas: BSW 1/8 minor printed .0903 (formula .0930) and BSF 7/16 minor printed .3363 (formula .3664) look like digit errors. A BSW row printed "4 3/4" carries the 5 in major diameter and is not used.

BF_BSF.title: British Threads - British Standard Fine (BSF table)
BF_BSF.note: Prints TPI, pitch, core (minor) diameter and tapping drills, 3/16 to 1 in. No standard number cited. Its 7/16 core .3663 agrees with the BS 84 profile, so the Engineers Edge .3363 is a digit error.

WIKI_BA.title: British Association screw threads (size table)
WIKI_BA.note: Names BS 93:2008. States pitch = 0.9^n mm, major diameter = 6 p^1.2 mm, both rounded to two significant figures, angle 47.5 deg, depth 0.6p, radius 0.18083p. Table printed for 0 to 10 BA and 25 BA only.

BF_BA.title: British Threads - BA (table, inch)
BF_BA.note: Prints diameters and pitch in inch, 0 to 16 BA. Its inch diameters differ slightly from the metric values converted (0 BA .2360 in against 6.0 mm = .2362 in), so only TPI is compared; diameters come from the BS 93 formula.

WIKI_MT.title: Machine taper (Morse, Jacobs, R8 and HSK tables)
WIKI_MT.note: Morse table: taper ratio, gauge diameter A (mm and in), half angle. Names ISO 296:1991, DIN 228-1, ISO 7388-1/-2, ASME B5.50, ISO 12164 and JIS B 6339 without current editions. R8 given in prose only.

LMS.title: Dimensions of standard tapers (Morse, Jacobs, Brown & Sharpe, Jarno)
LMS.note: Inch. Morse: large end, small end, length, taper per foot, taper per inch, angle from centre. Morse 4 1/2 printed with large end 1.5000 and taper per foot 0.6240; Wikipedia prints 1.4895 in and 1:19.128 (0.6274 per foot).

TNG.title: Taper specifications (NMTB, CAT/V-flange, ISO 7388-1/DIN 69871, BT)
TNG.note: Tables credited to Kennametal catalogue 7060 and to ANSI B5.50, ISO 7388-1, DIN 69871, JIS B 6339 and JMTBA AS-403. CAT and BT in inch with mm in brackets (inch used here); CAT 40 flange printed "2.500 (63.05)", where 2.500 in is 63.50 mm, so the mm figure is a digit error. The page warns its dimensions are not for part construction or inspection.

PARLEC.title: Parlec catalogue p. 6, CAT and BT taper specifications
PARLEC.note: Toolholder maker. Values to 2 decimals without units (inch). Threads printed with pitch ("M16 - 2.0", "5/8" - 11"); recorded as M16 and 5/8-11 for comparison.

notes.steep724: All three are 7:24 tapers (3.5 in per foot, included angle 16.594 deg) with the same gauge diameters; they differ in the flange, the drive slots and the retention knob. ISO 7388-1 (forms A/AD/AF, the DIN 69871 "SK" holder) and ISO 7388-2 (form J, the JIS B 6339 / MAS 403 "BT" holder) are metric; CAT (ASME B5.50, ISO 7388-1 form U) uses an inch thread. Retention knobs (pull studs): ISO 7388-3:2016 (forms AD, AF, UD, UF, JD, JF), ASME B5.50 for CAT and JIS B 6339 for BT. Knob profiles and angles differ between machine builders, so check the machine manual before ordering.
notes.morse: Morse tapers are self-holding (about 1:20, roughly 5/8 in per foot; each size has its own ratio). Gauge diameter = diameter at the gauge line (the large end of the socket). Current standard: ISO 296:1991 (self-holding tapers for tool shanks), with DIN 228-1 the matching German standard. Morse 4 1/2 is rare and the two publishers disagree on it. Included angle = 2 atan(taper per foot / 24).
notes.jacobs: Jacobs tapers hold drill chucks on arbors; they are not Morse tapers and the taper per foot differs between sizes (about 0.59 to 0.98 in per foot). Values as published for the Jacobs Chuck series; the drill chuck tapers of DIN 238 (B-series) are a different, metric family and are not listed here. The JT 6 and JT 33 sizes sit between JT 2 and JT 3 in diameter.
notes.hsk: HSK hollow taper shank with flange face contact. Current standard: ISO 12164-1:2023 (shanks of types A, AB, C, CB and EB); DIN 69893-1 is the original German standard. Size = flange diameter d1 in mm (HSK-A 63 has d1 = 63 mm). HSK holders are clamped from inside by the spindle's clamping mechanism, so there is no pull stud. Only one free publisher found so far for the taper diameters; check the holder maker's drawing.
notes.r8: R8 is a collet and toolholder taper used on knee mills (Bridgeport type), held by a 7/16-20 UNF drawbar. No international standard for R8 was found; dimensions are as published, from one source so far.
